items.title: Benmelstobart With or Without Anlotinib After Chemoradiotherapy for Unresectable Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: The R-ALPS Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Consolidation immunotherapy improves outcomes after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Disease progression remains common, and more effective consolidation strategies are needed.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of benmelstobart with or without anlotinib as consolidation therapy after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable stage III NSCLC.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter double-blind phase 3 randomized clinical trial took place at 42 centers in China from 2020 to 2023 among patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC without progression after concurrent or sequential chemoradiotherapy. In stage 1, patients were randomized 1:1:1 to 2 active regimens or placebo; in stage 2, additional patients were randomized 1:1 between the active regimens to power their direct comparison. Data cutoffs were November 30, 2023, for stage 1 and July 8, 2024, for the pooled analysis. Data analysis was performed from January 17 to March 23, 2025.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized to receive benmelstobart plus anlotinib, benmelstobart plus anlotinib placebo, or their matching placebos.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary end point was independent review committee (IRC)-assessed progression-free survival (PFS).
RESULTS: Of 553 participants (median [IQR] age, 62 [56-67] years; 495 male individuals [89.5%]), 390 were randomized in stage 1 and 163 in stage 2. In stage 1, median PFS was 15.1 months (95% CI, 9.4-21.7) with benmelstobart plus anlotinib, 9.7 months (95% CI, 6.0-34.4) with benmelstobart alone, and 4.2 months (95% CI, 3.2-6.8) with placebo. The hazard ratios (HRs) were 0.49 (95% CI, 0.36-0.66; P < .001) for benmelstobart plus anlotinib vs placebo and 0.53 (95% CI, 0.39-0.72; P < .001) for benmelstobart vs placebo. In the pooled stage 1 and 2 analysis, median PFS was 17.4 (95% CI, 12.5-24.8) months with benmelstobart plus anlotinib and 11.2 (95% CI, 7.0-20.7) months with benmelstobart alone (HR, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.63-1.08; P = .12). Grade 3 to 5 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 48.8%, 29.4%, and 19.7% in the benmelstobart plus anlotinib, benmelstobart alone, and placebo groups, respectively; grade 5 events occurred in 7.2%, 1.4%, and 1.5%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: This randomized clinical trial found that benmelstobart with or without anlotinib significantly improved PFS compared with placebo. Adding anlotinib did not significantly improve PFS compared with benmelstobart alone and increased severe and fatal treatment-related adverse events.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04325763.

items.title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: To our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival.
METHODS: This open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting.
FINDINGS: Between July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group.
INTERPRETATION: In this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX. Comparison of this promising new treatment strategy with contemporary total neoadjuvant therapy strategies is warranted.

items.title: Tozorakimab to Prevent COPD Exacerbations.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Many patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) have exacerbations despite receiving standard-of-care inhaled maintenance therapy. Dysregulated interleukin-33 signaling is implicated in the pathogenesis of COPD. Tozorakimab is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits the activity of interleukin-33.
METHODS: In two replicate phase 3 trials (OBERON and TITANIA), we enrolled adults with COPD who were current or former smokers and had a history of exacerbations in the previous year despite receiving stable standard-of-care inhaled maintenance therapy. There were no eligibility criteria related to blood eosinophil count. Patients were randomly assigned to receive add-on subcutaneous tozorakimab (300 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks for 52 weeks. items.title: Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing vs Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block and Preserved Left Ventricular Function: The LEAP-Block Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: For patients with atrioventricular block requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, the optimal pacing strategy to reduce heart failure (HF) and all-cause mortality remains uncertain. Robust comparative evidence on the clinical outcomes of left bundle-branch area pacing (LBBAP) vs right ventricular pacing (RVP) in this population is needed.
OBJECTIVE: To compare 24-month clinical outcomes of LBBAP vs RVP in patients with atrioventricular block and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF; ≥50%).
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: The LEAP-Block study was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, controlled, superiority trial conducted across 14 Chinese hospitals from January 2021 to August 2025, with last follow-up on June 3, 2025. Of 551 patients with LVEF 50% or greater requiring ventricular pacing who underwent eligibility assessment, 499 with anticipated ventricular pacing greater than 40% were randomized.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to LBBAP (n = 249) or RVP (n = 250).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary end point was a composite of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months. Secondary end points included pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and device-related complications.
RESULTS: The primary analysis included 482 patients (LBBAP, n = 242; RVP, n = 240; mean age, 67 years; 46% female). Acute procedure success was comparable between the 2 groups (LBBAP, 237/242 [97.9%] vs RVP, 239/240 [99.6%]; P = .22), with left bundle-branch capture confirmed in 188 of 236 patients (79.7%). LBBAP significantly reduced the primary end point vs RVP (2.4% vs 12.5%, respectively; absolute risk difference, -10.1% [95% CI, -16.8% to -3.4%]; P = .003). Among secondary outcomes, the LBBAP group had fewer HF events (3.4% vs 11.3%; -7.9% [95% CI, -13.0% to -2.8%]). No significant differences were observed in all-cause death, biventricular pacing upgrade, device-related complications, or pacing-induced cardiomyopathy. The 24-month Kaplan-Meier estimated cumulative incidence of the primary end point was 5.0% for LBBAP vs 13.2% for RVP (hazard ratio, 0.37 [95% CI, 0.19 to 0.73]; P = .004). LBBAP superiority was consistent across all prespecified subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Among patients with atrioventricular block and preserved LVEF requiring high-burden ventricular pacing, LBBAP was superior to RVP in reducing the risk of the composite end point of all-cause death, HF events, or upgrade to biventricular pacing at 24 months.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT04730921.

items.title: Immediate Ambulatory Electrocardiographic Monitoring in Syncope.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In patients with syncope who present to the emergency department for evaluation, diagnosing an underlying cardiac arrhythmia remains difficult.
METHODS: We conducted an open-label, randomized, controlled trial at 45 hospitals in the United Kingdom to assess the effects of 14-day cardiac monitoring on diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes among patients with syncope. Adults with syncope that remained unexplained after an evaluation in the emergency department were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo 14-day ambulatory electrocardiographic (ECG) monitoring (the intervention group) or to receive the standard care provided for patients with unexplained syncope at each participating site (the standard-care group). The primary outcome was the mean number of patient-reported episodes of syncope at 1 year.
RESULTS: A total of 2234 patients underwent randomization: 1123 were assigned to the intervention group and 1111 to the standard-care group. The mean age of the patients was 58.3 years, and 52.1% were male. After the exclusion of patients who did not complete any follow-up, a total of 1970 patients (1004 in the intervention group and 966 in the standard-care group) were included in the primary analysis. The mean (±SD) number of patient-reported syncope episodes at 1 year was 1.37±5.10 in the intervention group and 1.58±8.56 in the standard-care group (incidence rate ratio, 0.89; 95% confidence interval, 0.68 to 1.18; P = 0.42). A total of 49 adverse events were reported in the intervention group, and 8 adverse events were reported in the standard-care group, with 1 serious adverse event in each group.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with syncope that remained unexplained after evaluation in the emergency department, the use of 14-day ambulatory ECG monitoring did not result in significantly fewer patient-reported syncope episodes at 1 year than standard care. (Funded by the British Heart Foundation and National Health Service Research Scotland; ASPIRED ISRCTN Registry number, ISRCTN10278811.).

items.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant (castration-resistant) prostate cancer (TALAPRO-2): a biomarker analysis of circulating tumour DNA and cells for prognosis and molecular profiling.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The TALAPRO-2 trial showed improved radiographic progression-free survival and overall survival with first-line talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus placebo plus enzalutamide in patients with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (APMR; also referred to as castration-resistant prostate cancer) unselected for homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene alterations treated. We aimed to assess HRR gene alteration status agreement between prospective solid tumour tissue and circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) testing, the potential complementary value of prospective and retrospective ctDNA testing, and the prognostic utility of baseline ctDNA burden, changes in ctDNA burden, and circulating tumour cell (CTC) reductions.
METHODS: In TALAPRO-2, a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial, men aged 18 years or older (≥20 years in Japan) with asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic metastatic APMR prostate cancer and no previous life-prolonging systemic therapy for APMR disease were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive once daily, oral talazoparib 0·5 mg plus enzalutamide 160 mg or placebo plus enzalutamide and stratified by HRR gene alteration status and previous treatment for androgen pathway modulator-naive/sensitive disease. The sponsor, patients, and investigators were masked to allocation of talazoparib or placebo; enzalutamide was open label. In this exploratory analysis, HRR gene alteration status agreement was evaluated in the unselected intention-to-treat cohort between solid tumour tissue prospectively tested using a clinical trial assay based on FoundationOne CDx and retrospectively tested ctDNA samples, collected at screening and assessed using an assay based on FoundationOne Liquid CDx. Tumour burden was categorised as positive or negative (ctDNA tumour fraction detectable or not detectable). Reductions in CTCs, enumerated using CELLSEARCH, were defined as conversion (from five or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to four or fewer cells per 7·5 mL of blood) or CTC0 (from one or more cells per 7·5 mL of blood to zero). Radiographic progression-free survival was assessed for patients with baseline ctDNA positivity (positive vs negative) and for patients with ctDNA conversion and CTC conversion and CTC0 at week 9 (and week 17 for CTC conversion and CTC0) by treatment group. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrial.gov, NCT03395197 and is active, not recruiting.
FINDINGS: Between Jan 7, 2019, and Sept 17, 2020, 805 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned (402 to talazoparib plus enzalutamide; 403 to placebo plus enzalutamide); median follow-up for radiographic progression-free survival was 24·9 months (IQR 21·9-30·2) for the talazoparib group and 24·6 months (14·4-30·2) for the placebo group. A high concordance in HRR gene alteration status was observed between results from prospectively tested solid tumour tissue samples and retrospectively tested screening ctDNA samples (reported for 739 [92%] of 805 enrolled patients), with 84% (421 of 501) agreement in patients evaluable as either HRR-deficient or HRR-non-deficient by both tests. Median radiographic progression-free survival for positive versus negative ctDNA burden was 21·0 months (95% CI 16·5-not reached [NR]) versus NR (NR-NR), respectively (hazard ratio [HR] 2·46; 95% CI 1·68-3·60; p<0·0001) with talazoparib plus enzalutamide, and 11·0 months (8·4-13·8) versus 33·2 months (30·3-NR), respectively (HR 4·03; 2·85-5·72; p<0·0001) with placebo plus enzalutamide. In both groups, week 9 conversion from positive to negative ctDNA was prognostic of improved radiographic progression-free survival versus remaining ctDNA positive. Patients remaining ctDNA negative had more favourable radiographic progression-free survival versus conversion from positive to negative ctDNA. CTC conversion and CTC0 at week 9 were prognostic for radiographic progression-free survival benefit in both groups.
INTERPRETATION: Our results support broad prognostic utility of ctDNA burden and CTC enumeration in metastatic APMR prostate cancer, including in the context of poly(ADP) ribose polymerase inhibitor therapy.

items.title: B cell subsets are associated with durable responses in distinct cancer types after immune checkpoint inhibition.
items.abstract: B cells are a critical arm of the adaptive immune system. However, the impact of B cells and antibody responses on overall cancer survival remains understudied. Here, we report results from a prospective randomized phase 2 trial of 106 patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and identify that B cell antibody responses are associated with exceptional complete responses to ICI in certain cancer types. To further dissect the impact of B cell subtypes, we generated a comprehensive single-cell RNA sequencing database of intratumoral B cells in 12 tumor types from 152 patients. We found a context-dependent role for B cells, in which they are beneficial in certain cancer types and potentially unfavorable in others, with germinal center and memory B cells enriched in favorable prognosis cohorts and immunoglobulin A-positive plasma cells enriched in unfavorable prognosis cohorts. Depletion of B cells using rituximab in patients before surgery affected intratumoral T cell frequency and diversity. Furthermore, we show that B cells improve long-term overall survival even when T cell infiltrates are already high, indicating that a coordinated dual-arm T cell and B cell adaptive immune response is key to long-term tumor control. Overall, these results demonstrate that B cells and antibody responses in the proper context play an important role in durable complete responses in multiple tumor types.

items.title: Pazopanib alternating with bevacizumab in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to treatment: a multicentre, single-arm, phase 1/2 trial.
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) are considered the backbone for the treatment of metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. We hypothesise that the administration of bevacizumab during scheduled breaks in pazopanib (TKI) treatment can improve tolerability and prolong progression-free survival compared with historical controls.
METHODS: In this single-arm, phase 1/2 trial in five US academic cancer centres, patients (aged ≥18 years) with histologically confirmed metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 1 or less, and adequate organ functions were included. The phase 1 portion included patients with up to one previous therapy with high-dose IL-2 or an anti-PD-1 compound alone or in combination with a CTLA-4 inhibitor. The phase 2 portion enrolled only patients with treatment-naive metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma. The primary endpoint of phase 1 was to find the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D). We tested a novel regimen using four dose levels: oral pazopanib (600 or 800 mg daily on days 1-28, followed by a 7 day break) alternating with intravenous bevacizumab (5, 7·5, or 10 mg/kg, one on day 36 and one on day 50) on a 10-week cycle in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma naive to TKI treatment. The primary endpoint of phase 2 was median progression-free survival, assessed by a masked central statistician review. Dose selection (in patients who had completed 15 weeks) and activity (in patients who had completed one full 10-week cycle of the novel regimen) were analysed in the per-protocol population. Safety analyses included all patients who received any treatment. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01684397) and is ongoing but closed to new participants.
FINDINGS: Between Nov 21, 2012, and June 11, 2018, phase 1 enrolled 25 patients, with 18 patients evaluable for dose-limiting toxicity during the extended 15-week safety assessment period. The RP2D was established as pazopanib 800 mg daily (days 1-28) and bevacizumab 10 mg/kg on days 36 and 50 of a 10-week cycle. Between Jan 23, 2019, and Oct 19, 2023, phase 2 enrolled 53 patients, of whom 51 (including six from phase 1) were evaluable for activity and 59 were evaluable for safety. 36 (71%) patients were male and 15 (29%) were female, and 48 (94%) patients were White. 33 (65%) patients in phase 2 had favourable risk per the International Metastatic Renal Cell Carcinoma Database Consortium categories. After a median follow-up of 63·7 months (IQR 16·2-73·5), median progression-free survival was 24·8 months (95% CI 17·2-34·3). The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (20 [34%] of 59) and elevated aspartate aminotransferase (seven [12%]) and alanine aminotransferase (ten [17%]). Five (8%) patients discontinued the study for drug-related serious adverse events. No treatment-related deaths occurred.
INTERPRETATION: The phase 1 portion identified the safe RP2D. The phase 2 portion showed that this novel regimen has promising antitumour activity in patients with metastatic clear-cell renal cell carcinoma in the predominantly favourable risk group who are naive to treatment. Phase 3 randomised controlled trial data are needed to confirm these findings.

items.title: CPS + EG and Neo-Bioscore predict individual outcomes but not trial results after neoadjuvant therapy for early breast cancer.
items.abstract: CPS + EG and Neo-Bioscore are prognostic scores estimating the risk of recurrence after neoadjuvant chemotherapy for early breast cancer, but can they predict the long-term outcomes in a clinical trial? In this study, we assessed their surrogacy values at patient level and trial level for long-term outcomes, using data from 8,359 patients across nine neoadjuvant randomized trials conducted by the German Breast Group (GBG) and AGO-B study group. We found that at the patient level, both scores were significantly associated with outcomes, but at the trial level, the associations with distant disease-free survival (DDFS), invasive disease-free survival (iDFS), and overall survival (OS) were weak for both scores (R2 range = 0.03 to 0.24, with wide confidence intervals). Thus, our findings suggest that CPS + EG and Neo-Bioscore are not reliable surrogate endpoints for predicting long-term treatment benefit in neoadjuvant trials but remain valuable for estimating individual patients' residual risk after neoadjuvant treatments and guiding subsequent treatment decisions for early breast cancer patients.

items.title: Intermittent or Continuous Renal-Replacement Therapy in Acute Kidney Injury.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The preferred method of renal-replacement therapy for acute kidney injury in critically ill patients remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned critically ill adults with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy to undergo intermittent hemodialysis or continuous renal-replacement therapy as the initial treatment. The primary outcome was a major adverse kidney event - defined as death, dependence on renal-replacement therapy, or a serum creatinine concentration more than 25% above the baseline value - by day 90.
RESULTS: The trial was stopped early after sequential interim analyses showed a sustained signal of higher mortality with intermittent hemodialysis than with continuous renal-replacement therapy. A total of 554 patients underwent randomization, with 272 patients assigned to undergo intermittent hemodialysis and 282 to undergo continuous renal-replacement therapy; 535 patients (260 in the intermittent group and 275 in the continuous group) were included in the intention-to-treat population. A major adverse kidney event occurred by day 90 in 203 patients (78.1%) in the intermittent group and in 197 patients (71.6%) in the continuous group (adjusted absolute risk difference, 6.28 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.22 to 13.79). Death by day 90 occurred in 164 patients (63.1%) and in 147 patients (53.5%), respectively. Kaplan-Meier mortality estimates at day 90 were 63.3% and 53.6% (hazard ratio, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.04 to 1.63). The most common complication potentially related to acute kidney injury or renal-replacement therapy was hypotension, which occurred in 179 patients (68.8%) in the intermittent group and in 183 patients (66.5%) in the continuous group.
CONCLUSIONS: Among critically ill patients with acute kidney injury who had indications for renal-replacement therapy, intermittent hemodialysis as the initial treatment approach was not shown to be noninferior to continuous renal-replacement therapy with respect to major adverse kidney events by day 90 and was associated with higher mortality. (Funded by the French Ministry of Health; ICRAKI ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06032884.).

items.title: Efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid compared with sham for midportion Achilles tendinopathy (Inject trial): randomised controlled trial.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To test the efficacy and cost effectiveness of high volume injections with and without corticosteroid versus sham injection for midportion Achilles tendinopathy.
DESIGN: Single centred, participant and assessor masked, three arm randomised controlled trial (Inject trial).
SETTING: Community.
PARTICIPANTS: From 5 December 2019 and 24 July 2022, 192 adults (18 years or older) diagnosed with midportion Achilles tendinopathy were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to sham (n=64), high volume injection without corticosteroid (n=63), or high volume injection with corticosteroid (n=65).
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were allocated to sham injection (2-3 mL 0.5% bupivacaine hydrochloride), high volume injection with corticosteroid (50 mL saline and 0.5% bupivacaine with 25 mg hydrocortisone in the first 10 mL), or high volume injection with no corticosteroid (same solution but without hydrocortisone). They received the same exercise programme, education, and activity modification advice.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary clinical outcome was pain and disability using the validated VISA-A and the primary endpoint was at 52 weeks. The economic outcome was cost per quality-adjusted life-years from a societal perspective.
RESULTS: VISA-A data were obtained from 181 (94%) of 192 participants at 12 months. No clear differences were noted between sham and high volume injection either with (-3.5 (98.33% confidence interval -12.0 to 5.0)) or without corticosteroid (4.0 (-4.2 to 12.3)), and between the two injections (-7.5 (-15.3 to 0.3)), at 12 months. The point estimate was closest to the target difference for the comparison between injections and favoured the arm without steroid. The only differences observed on VISA-A at intermediate time points were a benefit for high volume with corticosteroid versus sham at six weeks (9.2 (1.5 to 16.9)) but worse outcomes for high volume injection with corticosteroid versus high volume injection with no corticosteroid at 26 weeks (-8.6 (-16.4 to -0.7)). The health economic analysis found high volume injection with corticosteroid to be less costly than the sham with similar effectiveness based on quality-adjusted life-years (>0.90 probability of being cost effective at $AUD50 000 and $100 000 willingness-to-pay thresholds). No serious trial related adverse events were recorded.
CONCLUSION: High volume injections with or without corticosteroids did not improve pain or disability compared with sham at 12 months. Although high volume injections with corticosteroid showed short term clinical benefit and potential reduction in healthcare costs over a year, they were associated with worse longer term clinical outcomes. The clinical data do not support routine use for high volume injections with corticosteroid for midportion Achilles tendinopathy.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry ACTRN12619001455156.

items.title: Surgical Margin and Risk of Local Recurrence in Children and Young Adults With Nonrhabdomyosarcoma Soft Tissue Sarcoma: A Nonrandomized Clinical Trial.
items.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: The extent of negative margin necessary to achieve a high rate of local tumor control in children and young adult patients with nonrhabdomyosarcoma soft tissue sarcomas (NRSTS) is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the impact of negative margin extent on local tumor control in children and young adult patients with NRSTS undergoing R0 resection as part of risk-adapted multimodality treatment.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter prospective clinical trial was conducted at Children's Oncology Group (COG) member sites from February 2007 through February 2012. Analysis was performed on the final dataset June 30, 2018, with a median follow-up of 6.2 years. Reviewers of margin status/extent were blinded to local control outcomes. Patients included 266 eligible/evaluable individuals younger than 30 years with nonmetastatic NRSTS who were enrolled in the COG ARST0332 trial and underwent upfront or delayed R0 resection as part of treatment. Patients who underwent an amputation or did not receive protocol-specified radiotherapy were excluded. These data were analyzed from January 2023 through July 2026.
INTERVENTION: Risk-adapted treatment included 3 patient groups with upfront or delayed surgery with or without radiation therapy with or without ifosfamide/doxorubicin chemotherapy, based on the extent of initial resection, surgical margin status, tumor size, and histologic grade.
MAIN OUTCOMES: Cumulative incidence of local recurrence based on treatment approach and surgical margin extent and outcomes after local recurrence.
RESULTS: Of 266 patients (median age 13.7 [range, 2.1-27.6] years; 138 female [52%] and 128 male [48%]) who underwent upfront (n = 207) or delayed (n = 59) R0 resection, 132 had measured surgical margins: 1 mm (n = 56), 2 to 5 mm (n = 50), or 6-mm or larger (n = 26). The 5-year cumulative incidence of local recurrence overall was 4.4%. Local recurrence occurred in 10 of 178 patients treated with surgery alone (5.6%) and 2 of 88 patients treated with surgery and chemoradiotherapy (2.3%). Among the 132 patients with measured surgical margins, the 5-year cumulative incidence of local recurrence was 4.9% for 1-mm margins, 2.0% for 2- to 5-mm margins, and 0% for 6-mm or larger margins. Local recurrence occurred in 10 of 178 (5.6%) patients with tumors smaller than 5 cm treated with margin-negative surgery alone, 1 of 29 (3.4%) patients with tumors larger than 5 cm treated with margin-negative surgery followed by chemoradiotherapy, and 1 of 59 (1.7%) patients with initially unresectable disease treated with neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. Five of 12 patients with local recurrence were alive without further disease progression.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this study, the local recurrence rate after R0 resection among children and young adult patients treated with risk-based therapy for nonmetastatic NRSTS was low, and some patients underwent successful salvage therapy with durable long-term disease control. Wider (>1 mm) negative margins further decrease local recurrence risk. Close surgical margins may be adequate in some clinical settings, particularly in the context of chemoradiotherapy, according to a risk-adapted approach.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT00346164.

items.title: In Vitro Fertilization or Intrauterine Insemination in Unexplained Infertility.
items.journal: The New England journal of medicine
items.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although international guidelines recommend intrauterine insemination (IUI) with ovarian stimulation as first-line treatment for unexplained infertility, evidence from comparisons of this method with in vitro fertilization (IVF) is limited.
METHODS: We conducted a sequential, multicenter, randomized, controlled trial involving couples with unexplained infertility. Stage 1 was a noninferiority comparison between IUI with ovarian stimulation (up to four cycles) and IVF (one complete cycle, with transfer of all embryos). After 7 months, couples without live birth or ongoing pregnancy could proceed to stage 2: couples in the IUI group could undergo up to two IVF cycles, and those in the IVF group could undergo one further IVF cycle. The primary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stage 1. Couples who were in stage 1 during lockdowns due to coronavirus disease 2019 were omitted from the analysis of the primary outcome. A secondary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stages 1 and 2. Live births were included in analyses if day 1 of the treatment cycle that led to pregnancy or day 1 of the last menstrual period before conception occurred within 7 months (stage 1) or 20 months (stage 2) after randomization. The noninferiority margin for the primary outcome was a between-group difference of 10 percentage points.
RESULTS: A total of 737 couples underwent randomization: 365 couples were assigned to undergo IUI with ovarian stimulation before IVF, and 372 were assigned to undergo first-line IVF (1 couple in the IVF group withdrew consent for the use of data). The primary-outcome analysis included 585 couples (288 in the IUI group and 297 in the IVF group). The cumulative live-birth rate from stage 1 was 31% (89 births among 288 couples) with IUI with ovarian stimulation and 55% (164 births among 297 couples) with IVF (adjusted risk difference, -24 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -31 to -16). The cumulative live-birth rate from stages 1 and 2 among all the couples who had undergone randomization and provided consent was 70% (257 births among 365 couples) and 71% (265 births among 371 couples), respectively (adjusted risk difference, 0 percentage points; 99% CI, -9 to 8). Overall, serious adverse events occurred in 6 couples in the IUI group and in 14 couples in the IVF group; most serious adverse events were related to oocyte retrieval or hyperstimulation.
CONCLUSIONS: In couples with unexplained infertility, treatment with four cycles of IUI with ovarian stimulation was not noninferior to treatment with one complete cycle of IVF with respect to the cumulative live-birth rate. (Funded by the Health Research Council of New Zealand and others; FIIX Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry number, ACTRN12619001003167.).

items.title: A Phase 2, Double-Blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Acmopatide (CT-868), a Fully Biased GLP-1/GIP Receptor Agonist, in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes and Overweight or Obesity.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of acmopatide, a signal-biased glucagon-like peptide 1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonist, in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) and overweight/obesity.
RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: In this phase 2, 16-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study, adults with T1D (HbA1c 7.0-10.0%; BMI ≥27 kg/m2) were randomized 1:1:1:1 to once-daily subcutaneous acmopatide (1.8, 4.1, or 6.6 mg) or volume-matched placebo. The primary end point was change from baseline (CFB) in HbA1c (%) at week 16; secondary end points included percent CFB in body weight and insulin dose.
RESULTS: Overall, 111 participants were randomized (placebo n = 29, acmopatide 1.8 mg n = 27, 4.1 mg n = 28, 6.6 mg n = 27). Mean (SD) baseline HbA1c was 7.5% (0.6), and mean BMI was 34.3 (5.6) kg/m2. Acmopatide improved HbA1c (least squares [LS] mean CFB -0.4 to -0.6% vs. -0.3% with placebo; nominally significant placebo-adjusted difference for 4.1 mg: -0.3% [90% CI -0.6 to -0.1]; P = 0.020). HbA1c <7.0% was achieved by 55.6% of participants receiving acmopatide 4.1 mg vs. 33.3% receiving placebo. Acmopatide-treated participants demonstrated reductions in body weight (LS mean CFB -3.3 to -6.7% vs. 0.3% with placebo; all P < 0.01), total daily insulin dose (-3.4 to -14.9% more than placebo for acmopatide 4.1 and 6.6 mg), and mean systolic blood pressure (-3.1 to -8.4 mmHg vs. -3.3 mmHg with placebo). Adverse events were primarily gastrointestinal. No diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) or severe hypoglycemia events occurred.
CONCLUSIONS: In adults with T1D and overweight/obesity, acmopatide was associated with improved glycemic control and clinically meaningful weight loss without DKA or severe hypoglycemia events.

items.title: Comparative effectiveness of three splints for rehabilitation after finger flexor tendon repair (FIRST): randomised controlled trial.
items.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the clinical effectiveness of three splints after repair of zone 1 and 2 flexor tendons: forearm based (long), Manchester short (short), and relative motion flexion (mini) splints.
DESIGN: Prospective, randomised, parallel group, pragmatic, superiority, clinical trial.
SETTING: 26 UK hospitals.
PARTICIPANTS: 430 participants (aged ≥16 years) requiring rehabilitation after primary repair of zone 1 and 2 flexor tendons in one or two fingers of the hand according to British Society for Surgery of the Hand guidelines.
INTERVENTIONS: Participants were randomly assigned 1:1:1 to the long, short, or mini splint. Splints were worn continuously for five weeks and intermittently for a further week at night and in vulnerable situations such as public environments. Masking participants was not possible owing to the nature of the intervention.
MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was the mean post-randomisation score on the patient-rated wrist and hand evaluation (PRWHE) instrument at 6, 12, 26, and 52 weeks, analysed by intention to treat.
RESULTS: 430 participants were randomised to the long splint (n=143), short splint (n=140), or mini splint (n=147) and 403 were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. Adherence, defined as wearing the splint for a minimum of five weeks, was 83% (118/143) for the long splint, 76% (106/140) for the short splint, and 78% (115/147) for the mini splint. Mean post-randomisation PRWHE scores were 24.5 (standard deviation 15.5) in the long splint group, 23.5 (16.7) in the short splint group, and 22.4 (15.0) in the mini splint group, with adjusted between group differences of 0.3 (98.3% confidence interval -4.0 to 4.6, P=0.88) for the long versus short splint, 2.3 (-1.9 to 6.5, P=0.19) for the long versus mini splint, and 2.0 (-2.2 to 6.3, P=0.25) for the short versus mini splint. Serious adverse event rates occurred in 10% (14/143) of participants in the long splint group, 11% (15/140) in the short splint group, and 11% (16/147) in the mini splint group.
CONCLUSION: This trial found no statistically significant difference in clinical effectiveness between the long, short, and mini splint. Apart from some small differences, secondary outcomes were comparable across all three groups.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ISRCTN Registry ISRCTN10236011.
